findings.recommendation: Fail to start when REDIS_PASSWORD is absent rather than substituting a literal, and treat the committed value as burned.

triage.reason: The fallback is a literal in the tree, not a placeholder that would fail loudly.
The same connection object serves the production scripts at package.json:8-9; no build step replaces it.
It is not defence in depth: it is the only credential on the queue.

findings.unaided_label: hardcoded Redis password fallback

findings.title: The production API task role is given AdministratorAccess
findings.evidence: environments.ts:26-30 maps tier 'ops' to the AWS managed policy AdministratorAccess. prod sets apiTier: 'ops' (environments.ts:68), and attachTierPolicy (lib/constructs/service-role.ts:43-46) attaches ManagedPolicy.fromAwsManagedPolicyName(policyName) to the role every ServiceRole builds. api-stack.ts:33-36 constructs that role as the taskRole of the Fargate task definition (api-stack.ts:46) for the internet-facing service behind the ALB at api-stack.ts:76-78. The comments at environments.ts:28 and 66-67 explain the intent: the production API also runs migrations and break-glass tooling.
findings.impact: The credentials of an internet-facing HTTP service are AWS administrator in the production account. Any RCE, SSRF to the task metadata endpoint, or dependency compromise in that container becomes full control of the account - IAM, data, backups and logs - with no further escalation step. The narrow grants the stack carefully adds beside it (grantArtifacts, grantQueue, secret.grantRead at api-stack.ts:39-41) are subsumed and meaningless.
findings.recommendation: Give the API task role only the grants the stack already attaches and delete the tier mechanism, or at minimum map 'ops' to a scoped customer-managed policy. Migrations and break-glass belong to a separate role assumed by a human or a pipeline with MFA and session logging, not to the request-serving task.

triage.reason: No condition, permissions boundary or SCP appears anywhere in beacon-cdk/; the role is created at service-role.ts:23-26 with no boundary and the managed policy is attached unconditionally.
The intent is declared in the comments, but nothing bounds it: the same role serves every request on the public listener.
prod is a first-class entry selected by BEACON_ENV at bin/beacon.ts:14; this is the shipped production configuration.

findings.unaided_label: prod apiTier 'ops' -> AdministratorAccess on the task role

findings.title: The production artifact bucket is anonymously readable, and it holds rendered documents and tenant exports
findings.evidence: prod sets assetsPublic: true (environments.ts:64) and data-stack.ts:28-32 passes it as publicRead. bucket.ts:33-40 then replaces BLOCK_ALL with a BlockPublicAccess that leaves blockPublicPolicy and restrictPublicBuckets false, and bucket.ts:55-64 attaches a policy granting s3:GetObject to iam.AnyPrincipal() over arnForObjects('*') - the entire bucket, not a prefix. The comment directly above the construction states what is in that bucket: data-stack.ts:26-27, "one bucket holds everything the platform produces: the brand assets the CDN pulls, the rendered documents and the tenant data exports".
findings.impact: Every rendered tenant document and every data export in the production account is readable by anonymous callers, with only object-key knowledge standing in the way, and object keys are structured and enumerable via ListBucket for anyone who obtains that grant. The intended public surface is the brand assets; the policy's scope is the whole bucket.
findings.recommendation: Split the buckets: one public origin bucket for brand assets, one blocked bucket for documents and exports. If they must share, scope the AnyPrincipal statement to arnForObjects('public/*') and keep blockPublicPolicy true elsewhere. Prefer a CloudFront origin access identity over anonymous s3:GetObject entirely.

triage.reason: The intended exposure is the CDN's brand assets (environments.ts:63, bucket.ts:7), and the grant written is arnForObjects('*'), which is wider than the intent by exactly the sensitive content.
data-stack.ts:26-27 names rendered documents and tenant data exports as residents of this bucket.
The public-access block that would compensate is deliberately relaxed for this case at bucket.ts:37-38.

findings.unaided_label: publicRead bucket policy grants AnyPrincipal GetObject over the whole bucket

findings.title: Bastion SSH is open to the entire internet in dev, and the environment picker silently falls back to dev
findings.evidence: environments.ts:36 sets adminCidrs: ['0.0.0.0/0'] for dev. network-stack.ts:52-58 loops over cfg.adminCidrs and adds an ingress rule on tcp/22 from each, so the bastion accepts SSH from anywhere. The bastion security group is in turn allowed into Postgres on 5432 (network-stack.ts:81-85). pickEnv (environments.ts:82-84) returns dev for any name it does not recognise, including undefined - so bin/beacon.ts:14, which reads BEACON_ENV with a context fallback, resolves to dev whenever the variable is unset or misspelled.
findings.impact: A world-reachable SSH endpoint that fronts the database subnet, in an account where the same configuration also makes the artifact bucket public (assetsPublic: true, environments.ts:37) and removal policies destructive. The fail-open picker means a pipeline typo deploys that posture rather than failing.
findings.recommendation: Replace the 0.0.0.0/0 entry with the real operator ranges, or drop the bastion in favour of SSM Session Manager, which needs no ingress at all. Make pickEnv throw on an unknown or missing name instead of returning dev.

triage.reason: dev is a deployable environment with its own account (environments.ts:34) and is the value pickEnv returns by default, so this configuration ships.
The comment at environments.ts:8 says adminCidrs are the ranges operators reach the bastion from; 0.0.0.0/0 is not a range, it is the absence of one.
No NACL, managed firewall or SSM-only policy appears in beacon-cdk/ to compensate.

findings.unaided_label: dev adminCidrs 0.0.0.0/0 on tcp/22 + pickEnv defaults to dev

findings.title: The artifact grant is called without the prefix the helper exists to enforce
findings.evidence: grantArtifacts (service-role.ts:52-70) takes a prefix parameter defaulting to '' and its doc comment (service-role.ts:48-51) says to pass the prefix the service writes under "so the grant stays scoped to it". api-stack.ts:39 calls grantArtifacts(serviceRole.role, props.artifacts.bucket) with two arguments, so prefix is '' and the statements become s3:GetObject/PutObject/DeleteObject on arnForObjects('*') plus s3:ListBucket with s3:prefix '*'. The bucket is the shared one that, per data-stack.ts:26-27, holds every tenant's documents and exports.
findings.impact: The API task can read, overwrite and delete every object belonging to every tenant, and enumerate the whole bucket. A defect in one tenant's request path becomes a cross-tenant write or a mass deletion, and there is no isolation left to fall back on.
findings.recommendation: Pass the service's prefix (grantArtifacts(role, bucket, 'renders/')) and give the export path its own. Split DeleteObject out entirely unless the service genuinely deletes.

triage.reason: There is no bucket policy or permissions boundary narrowing it; bucket.ts adds only the public-read statement, which widens rather than narrows.
The default parameter is not an implicit scope: '' expands to arnForObjects('*') at service-role.ts:60.
Least privilege here is load-bearing - it is the only tenant isolation on the object store.

findings.unaided_label: grantArtifacts called with no prefix

findings.title: The production database is created with publiclyAccessible: true
findings.evidence: data-stack.ts:60 sets publiclyAccessible: true on the RDS instance for every environment, and the comment at data-stack.ts:58-59 gives the reason: an analytics warehouse in a separate account pulls nightly over the public endpoint. The instance is otherwise placed in PRIVATE_ISOLATED subnets (data-stack.ts:48) and its security group (network-stack.ts:71-85) admits only the service and bastion groups - so the flag contradicts the placement, and the stated cross-account use cannot work without also opening that security group, which is the change this comment invites.
findings.impact: The instance is assigned a public DNS name and is one security-group edit away from being reachable from the internet, in an account whose bastion is already open to 0.0.0.0/0 in the dev configuration. It also removes the defence in depth that made the isolated subnet placement meaningful.
findings.recommendation: Set publiclyAccessible: false and give the warehouse a private path - VPC peering, PrivateLink, or a snapshot share into the analytics account. If a public endpoint is genuinely required, it needs its own justification, source-restricted ingress and enforced TLS, recorded as an accepted risk with an owner.

triage.reason: The security group compensates today (network-stack.ts:76-85 admits two SGs only), which is why this is medium and not high - but the flag itself is the defect and the comment describes traffic that requires opening it.
The intent is stated but unbounded: no source range, no PrivateLink and no condition accompanies it.
The flag is unconditional - it is not gated on cfg.ephemeral like multiAz, backupRetention and deletionProtection beside it.

findings.unaided_label: RDS publiclyAccessible: true

findings.title: The API container is configured for wildcard CORS with credentials
findings.evidence: api-stack.ts:53-61 injects CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN: '*' together with CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS: 'true' into the task environment, with the comment at api-stack.ts:57-58 explaining that the origin cannot be pinned because browsers hit the API from every tenant subdomain and from an embedded widget. Browsers reject the literal pair, so an implementation that honours both settings has to reflect the request origin - which is precisely the pattern the edge-relay nginx configuration in this same tree implements (edge-relay/nginx/relay.conf:39-40).
findings.impact: If the application reflects the origin to satisfy this configuration, any site can read authenticated API responses with the victim's credentials attached. The configuration expresses the intent that produces that outcome, and the widget requirement it cites is the standing reason not to fix it.
findings.recommendation: Replace the wildcard with an allowlist the application checks by exact match, generated from the tenant subdomain registry, and keep credentials only for those origins. For the embedded widget, use a token in the request rather than an ambient cookie so no credentialed cross-origin read is needed.

triage.reason: The application image beacon/api:1.12.0 (api-stack.ts:50) is not in this tree, so how it interprets these two variables cannot be established here. The declared configuration is the artifact I have; per the triage rules the UNKNOWN caps this at probable.
The API is authenticated (the task also receives DATABASE_SECRET at api-stack.ts:62-64), so its responses are not identical for every caller.
The setting is the deployed configuration, not a test value.

findings.unaided_label: CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN '*' with CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS true
